desc: Ideation: derive telescoping identity f(s) = s − Σ_{t=1}^{v2(s)} s/2^t, reducing problem to per-t residue-class aggregation mod 2^t; verified on sample 1 (answer 5).

Implement the telescoping solution in Python: read N and A; compute S_total = (N+1)*sum(A); for t = 1..24 (while (1<<t) <= 2*max(A)): build dict mapping residue mod 2^t → [count, sum], compute S_t from residue-class pairs (r, r' = (-r) mod M) with r<r' contributing c[r]*w[r']+c[r']*w[r] and r==r' contributing (c[r]+1)*w[r]; answer = S_total − Σ S_t >> t. Fast I/O via sys.stdin.buffer.

Double-check edge cases: N=1 verified (answer = f(2A_1), e.g. A=[4] → 1); t range 1..24 correct since max sum 2·10^7 < 2^25; S_t divisible by 2^t by construction so >> is exact; Sample 2 hand-verified (384); performance ~5×10^6 dict ops, memory O(N).
